policy.missing_data: Missing or out-of-domain values remain null. They are never silently converted to zero, a global median, or a neighboring-region value for a physical forecast.
policy.provenance: Every imported dataset must retain its stable identifier, version, DOI or URL, publication date, observation period, retrieval date, license, units, reference frame, spatial resolution, uncertainty description, and geographic validity.
policy.independence: Sources that reuse the same observations, inversion, catalog, or model family must be linked by dependency_group. They are not counted as independent confirmations.
policy.regional_use: Regional models may refine the global baseline only inside their documented domain and only for variables they actually constrain.
policy.historical_replay: A modern dataset cannot be presented as information available at a past forecast cutoff. Store publication/release date separately from observation epoch and model epoch.

sources.name: USGS ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat)
sources.scope: Global, with contributing-network and time-dependent completeness differences
sources.temporal_coverage: Event- and contributor-dependent; query and raw response must be frozen per run
sources.spatial_resolution: Event-level; uncertainty depends on contributing network and event
sources.uncertainty: Use event/product uncertainty where supplied; do not assume uniform global completeness
limitations: Catalog entries and preferred products can be revised
Historical versions are not fully reconstructible from a current query
Finite-fault and moment-tensor products are available only for some events
sources.license: Review source and product-specific terms before redistribution

sources.name: ISC-GEM Global Instrumental Earthquake Catalogue v13.0
sources.scope: Global large and significant instrumental earthquakes; magnitude threshold and coverage depend on region and period
sources.spatial_resolution: Event-level; standardized location method with reported focal-parameter uncertainties
sources.uncertainty: Catalog includes uncertainties; supplementary catalog identifies events with higher location or magnitude uncertainty
limitations: Not a complete small-earthquake catalog
Not a real-time feed
Versioned release should be frozen for reproducible historical baselines

sources.name: Global Centroid Moment Tensor (GCMT) catalog
sources.scope: Global moderate-to-large earthquakes represented in GCMT
sources.temporal_coverage: Catalog archive currently pinned in the repository runner; exact end date must be stored with each downloaded snapshot
sources.uncertainty: Use source-provided quality/uncertainty where available; two nodal planes are alternative hypotheses, not two simultaneous ruptures
limitations: Magnitude and event selection thresholds limit completeness
NDK analysis timestamp is not guaranteed public-release timestamp
sources.license: Check GCMT terms for the downloaded release

sources.name: NNR-MORVEL56 plate angular velocities
sources.temporal_coverage: Geological long-term average; not a contemporaneous GNSS velocity field
sources.uncertainty: Use published covariance/uncertainty when imported; the current repository JSON stores angular velocities but not their covariance
limitations: Rigid-plate approximation does not resolve distributed deformation inside complex plate-boundary zones
Plate code mapping must be explicit

sources.name: Bird PB2002 plate-boundary geometry
sources.scope: Global plate-boundary linework and generalized boundary classes
sources.temporal_coverage: Static compilation; publication/model epoch must be retained
sources.spatial_resolution: Generalized boundary polylines, not fault-segment inventory
sources.uncertainty: No per-segment uncertainty is currently propagated
limitations: A boundary line is not necessarily the active seismogenic fault
Line orientation and generalized type cannot uniquely define local receiver strike, dip, and rake

sources.name: GEM Global Strain Rate Model v2.1
sources.scope: Global model; plate-boundary deformation is resolved where geodetic data support it, with other areas represented as rigid plate caps
sources.temporal_coverage: Published 2014; model epoch and input velocity time spans must be retained
sources.spatial_resolution: Deforming grid reported at 0.25 degree longitude by 0.2 degree latitude; resolution and data density vary
sources.uncertainty: Use signal-to-noise and model uncertainty products where available
limitations: Not a current 2026 GNSS solution
Only about 14 percent of Earth's surface is allowed to deform in the model; the rest is represented by rigid spherical caps
Open download has non-commercial/share-alike license restrictions
sources.license: The exact GSRM_average_strain_v2.1.txt asset used by the Bird GEAR1 archive declares CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (unported); preserve this asset-specific license and verify permissions before redistribution or commercial use

sources.name: GEM Global Active Faults Database
sources.scope: Global compilation from regional fault databases and published sources; heterogeneous regional completeness
sources.temporal_coverage: Version-dependent; pin exact Git commit or release
sources.spatial_resolution: Fault traces with region-dependent mapping scale
sources.uncertainty: Must be derived from source region/publication; do not assume one global positional accuracy
limitations: Known geographic gaps and heterogeneous source scales
Fault trace alone does not provide full 3-D geometry or locking
sources.license: Check the current repository/data license before redistribution

sources.name: USGS Slab2
sources.spatial_resolution: Nominal 0.05 degree source grids; effective resolution and uncertainty vary by region
sources.uncertainty: Use published regional uncertainty and model documentation when available
limitations: Does not describe all active crustal faults or all back-arc thrusts
Must not be substituted for receiver-fault geometry outside its intended interface
A missing grid cell means unknown, not zero depth or zero stress
sources.license: USGS data; retain attribution and source version

sources.name: Coupling Cloud
sources.scope: Published megathrust coupling models in selected subduction margins; coverage is not global and varies by model
sources.temporal_coverage: Each contributing model has its own GNSS observation period and publication date; preserve these separately
sources.spatial_resolution: Dataset-specific interface meshes or projected grids; do not imply one common resolution
sources.uncertainty: Model-specific; use original model and publication uncertainty, not only the harmonized raster
limitations: Models differ in assumptions, inversion methods, geometry and parameterization
Multiple models may use overlapping GNSS observations
Must not average incompatible variables or count duplicate datasets as independent evidence
sources.license: Per dataset/source; verify original publication/data license before reuse

sources.name: Li et al. — Slip deficit rate and seismic potential on crustal faults in Tibet
sources.scope: Tibetan Plateau and surrounding continental China GNSS region; 263 crustal faults represented by 383 segments
sources.temporal_coverage: Updated interseismic GNSS velocity solution; exact observation periods must be read from the dataset metadata
sources.spatial_resolution: Fault-segment model, 383 segments; strain grids and GNSS station geometry are source-specific
sources.uncertainty: Paper reports posterior slip-deficit uncertainty; preserve segment-wise posterior samples or summary intervals
limitations: Do not equate accumulated moment budget with short-term earthquake probability
Fault-plane geometry includes simplifying assumptions; assess the segment closest to each forecast region
Check event chronology and historical availability before a hindcast
sources.license: Zenodo dataset record; verify the version-specific license

sources.name: Zhao et al. — Interseismic Coupling Along the Java-Timor Subduction-Collision Zone at East Indonesia
sources.scope: Java-Timor subduction-collision zone, including Java-Timor megathrust and Flores-Wetar back-arc thrust
sources.temporal_coverage: Model-specific GNSS and focal mechanism observation periods; preserve original metadata
sources.spatial_resolution: Three-dimensional interface/fault model; regional resolving power differs along strike
sources.uncertainty: Use source posterior/uncertainty and resolution tests; some eastern sectors have weaker constraint
limitations: Do not transfer coupling values across poorly resolved gaps
Back-arc thrust and megathrust are separate receiver systems
Coupling measures interseismic kinematics, not a deterministic short-term clock
sources.license: Check original dataset and article terms

sources.name: Peter Bird — Kinematic and dynamic modeling of lithosphere deformation: Tools and results
sources.scope: Includes source code, input/output examples and reproduction materials for GEAR1, SHIFT_GSRM and other deformation models
sources.temporal_coverage: Archive published 2025-11-04; contains historical model inputs and outputs. Exact epoch is file-specific.
sources.spatial_resolution: GEAR1 published CSEP forecast uses a global 0.1 degree grid; other data files have file-specific grids/resolution
sources.uncertainty: Must use original file metadata and source paper; archive does not make all included models equally certain
limitations: Archive is a reproduction resource, not a modern updated GEAR1 model
GEAR1 is a static long-term shallow seismicity forecast, not a short-term aftershock model
Verify per-file license and third-party notices before redistribution or commercial use
Original Fortran tools may require compiler/library adaptation
sources.license: Verify Dryad dataset terms and any included third-party file notices before redistribution; GSRM v2.1 has separate GEM license conditions
